lessons.title: A dialogue about a message
lessons.objective: Carry out a dialogue on a familiar theme: passing on a message.
lessons.course:
In a dialogue, two people speak in turn. They ask questions, answer, check that they understood and close politely.
Useful phrases: “Can I take a message?”, “Could you repeat, please?”, “I will tell her.”, “Thank you for calling.”

support.title: Dialogue
support.text:
Tabi: Hello, this is Tabi. Can I speak to Mrs Ngwa?
Ngum: She is not at home. Can I take a message?
Tabi: Yes, please. Tell her the meeting is on Friday at four.
Ngum: Friday at four. I will tell her.
Tabi: Thank you. Goodbye!

lessons.model: Two adults act the dialogue with toy phones; the child notes the message.
lessons.guided: Act the dialogue in pairs, then change the day and time of the meeting.
lessons.exercise: What do we say when we did not hear well?
lessons.remediation: Act only the first two lines, then add the others.
lessons.transfer: Take a real message for someone at home and pass it on.
lessons.materials: Two toy phones, paper for the message.

practice.prompt: Put the dialogue in order.
items: Can I speak to Mrs Ngwa?
She is not at home. Can I take a message?
Tell her the meeting is on Friday at four.
practice.answer: ask, take a message, give the message, promise.

practice.prompt: What is the message?
choices: The meeting is on Friday at four.
practice.answer: The meeting is on Friday at four.

practice.prompt: Listen and say the message you have to pass on.
practice.listen: Please tell Papa that the mechanic will bring the car back on Saturday morning.
practice.answer: The mechanic will bring the car back on Saturday morning.

lessons.title: A prose passage: the tortoise and the message
lessons.objective: Read a short prose passage, put oneself in the place of a character and deduce the moral.
lessons.course: A prose passage is written in ordinary sentences and paragraphs, not in lines like a poem. Tales often have animal characters who teach a lesson.

support.title: Klassia tale
support.text: Long ago, the king of the animals had to send an important message to the next village. The proud hare said, “I am the fastest. I will carry it.” He ran off, but he stopped to eat sweet berries, then he slept under a tree. The tortoise also set off, slowly but without stopping. When the hare woke up, it was night. The tortoise had already delivered the message, and the villages came to the meeting on time.

lessons.model: The adult reads the tale aloud with expression and asks: “Who was faster? Who arrived first? Why?”
lessons.guided: Read the tale silently. Say how the hare felt at the beginning and at the end. Find the moral.
lessons.remediation: Read the tale paragraph by paragraph with the adult.
lessons.transfer: Ask an elder for a tale with a moral and retell it.

practice.prompt: What is the moral of the tale?
choices: Steady effort wins; pride can make us fail.
practice.answer: Steady effort wins; pride can make us fail.
practice.explanation: The tortoise never stopped; the hare was proud.

practice.prompt: Put the events in order.
practice.answer: king, hare runs, hare sleeps, tortoise delivers.

practice.prompt: Why did the hare not deliver the message?
practice.answer: Because he stopped to eat and slept.
accept: he stopped to eat and slept
Because he stopped to eat and slept

lessons.title: Writing a paragraph
lessons.objective: Write a paragraph with a topic sentence and supporting sentences.
lessons.course:
A paragraph is a group of sentences about one idea. The topic sentence gives the idea. The supporting sentences give details or examples. The paragraph starts on a new line, a little to the right (indentation).
Example of topic sentence: “The telephone is very useful in my family.”
lessons.model: The adult writes: “The telephone is very useful in my family. My father calls his customers. My mother sends money to Grandma. I call my aunt on her birthday.”
lessons.guided: Choose a topic sentence about communication. Add three supporting sentences. Indent the first line.
lessons.exercise: What is the first sentence of a paragraph called?
lessons.remediation: Start from a given topic sentence and add one detail at a time.
lessons.transfer: Write a paragraph about the radio or the television at home.

practice.prompt: Write a paragraph of four sentences about the telephone.
practice.answer: A topic sentence and three supporting sentences.

practice.prompt: Which sentence could be a topic sentence?
choices: Radios bring news to every village.
practice.answer: Radios bring news to every village.
practice.explanation: A topic sentence gives the main idea.

practice.prompt: Put the paragraph in order.
items: The telephone is very useful in my family.
My mother sends money to Grandma.

lessons.title: Kinds of sentences, conjunctions and punctuation
lessons.objective: Build declarative, interrogative and exclamatory sentences, join ideas with conjunctions and punctuate correctly.
lessons.course:
A declarative sentence gives information and ends with a full stop: The letter arrived. An interrogative sentence asks a question and ends with a question mark: Did the letter arrive? An exclamatory sentence shows strong feeling and ends with an exclamation mark: What good news!
Conjunctions join words or sentences: and, but, or, so, because. We use a capital letter at the start of a sentence and for names.
lessons.model: The adult writes three sentences about a letter and points to the three end marks.
lessons.guided: Change a declarative sentence into a question and an exclamation. Join two short sentences with a conjunction.
lessons.remediation: Sort sentence cards by their end mark.
lessons.transfer: Write one sentence of each kind about a phone call.

practice.prompt: Complete with the right conjunction.
practice.text: I called Grandma [[but]] she did not answer, [[so]] I sent a message.
practice.explanation: but shows a contrast; so shows a result.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is exclamatory?
practice.explanation: It shows strong feeling and ends with !

practice.prompt: Match each sentence with its kind.
pairs: The phone is on the table.

lessons.title: The 13 lunar months and the 12 calendar months
lessons.objective: Compare the lunar months and the calendar months and use both to place events.
lessons.course:
A lunar month is the time from one new moon to the next: about 29 or 30 days. There are about 13 lunar months in a year. Many traditional and religious calendars use the moon.
The calendar we use at school has 12 months of 28 to 31 days.
lessons.model: The adult shows the moon over a month: new moon, half moon, full moon, then new moon again after about 29 days.
lessons.guided: Observe the moon for a few evenings and draw its shape. Compare: how many lunar months, how many calendar months?
lessons.exercise: About how many days is a lunar month?
lessons.remediation: Use a calendar with moon pictures.
lessons.transfer: Ask an elder how the moon was used to mark time.

practice.prompt: How many calendar months are in a year?
About how many lunar months are in a year?
Which one marks a lunar month?
choices: from one new moon to the next
practice.answer: from one new moon to the next
practice.explanation: The moon’s cycle is about 29 days.

lessons.title: Coordinates on a grid
lessons.objective: Locate and plot points on a grid using coordinates (across, then up).
lessons.course:
On a grid, a point is given by two numbers in brackets: (across, up). (3, 2) means 3 squares across, then 2 squares up. We always go across first.
Coordinates help to send exact positions, for example on a map or in a message.
lessons.model: The adult places a dot at (4, 1) on squared paper: “four across, one up.”
lessons.guided: Plot five points and join them to make a shape. Send the coordinates of your shape to a friend who draws it.
lessons.exercise: Which number do we read first in (5, 2)?
lessons.remediation: Use a 5 × 5 grid and say “across, then up”.
lessons.transfer: Make a treasure map with coordinates.

practice.prompt: A point is 2 across and 4 up. Write its coordinates.
Is (3, 1) the same point as (1, 3)?
Plot the points (1, 1), (4, 1), (4, 3), (1, 3) and join them. What shape is it?
practice.explanation: 4 points with right angles: a rectangle.

lessons.title: Factors and multiples up to 50
lessons.objective: Find the factors of numbers up to 50 and recognise multiples.
lessons.course:
A factor divides a number exactly. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12 (1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4).
A multiple is the result of multiplying: 24 is a multiple of 6 because 6 × 4 = 24.
lessons.model: The adult arranges 18 phone cards in equal rows: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.
lessons.guided: Arrange counters in rectangles to find all the factors of 16 and 20.
lessons.remediation: Use the multiplication table to find pairs.
lessons.transfer: Find all the ways to arrange 24 chairs in equal rows.

practice.prompt: How many factors does 12 have?
Which number is a factor of 20?
Is 35 a multiple of 7? Answer yes or no.

lessons.title: A shopping bill up to 1 000 francs
lessons.objective: Prepare and check a shopping bill and manage a budget up to 1 000 frs.
lessons.course:
A bill lists each item, its quantity, its price and the total. Quantity × price = cost of the item. We add the costs to get the total, then compare with the money we have.
Being honest with money means checking bills and giving back extra change.
lessons.model: Bill: 2 exercise books × 150 frs = 300 frs; 1 pen × 100 frs = 100 frs; 1 phone credit card = 500 frs. Total: 900 frs. Money: 1 000 frs. Change: 100 frs.
lessons.guided: Prepare a bill for three school items. Check the total and the change.
lessons.exercise: 3 pencils at 50 frs each. What is the cost?
lessons.remediation: Use one item per line with quantity 1 first.
lessons.transfer: With an adult, check a real receipt.

practice.prompt: 4 exercise books at 125 frs each. Cost in frs?
Total of 300 frs + 100 frs + 500 frs?
The seller gives you 200 frs change instead of 100 frs. What do you do?

lessons.title: Telephones, radio, television and cameras
lessons.objective: Identify telecommunication tools, make a model and use devices responsibly.
lessons.course:
Telecommunication tools send sounds, pictures and words far away: the telephone, the radio, the television, the camera, the fax machine and the computer.
We use them responsibly: we ask permission, we respect privacy, we do not share other people’s photos without their agreement, and we keep devices dry and charged safely.
lessons.model: The adult makes a “string phone” with two tins and a string: the sound travels along the string.
lessons.guided: Make a string phone and talk with a friend. Then sort pictures: tools that send sound, pictures, or both.
lessons.exercise: Which tool sends both sound and pictures?
lessons.remediation: Work with the radio (sound) and the camera (pictures) first.
lessons.transfer: Ask permission before taking a photo of someone.
lessons.materials: Two tins, string, pictures of devices.

practice.prompt: Match each device with what it sends or records.
practice.answer: radio: sound; camera: pictures; television: sound and pictures.

practice.prompt: Before taking a photo of a friend, what do we do?
In a string phone, what carries the sound?
practice.explanation: The sound travels along the tight string.

lessons.title: Quel temps fait-il ? Quelle heure est-il ?
lessons.objective: Parler de la météo et de l’heure, et utiliser aujourd’hui, hier et demain.
lessons.course:
Pour la météo : « Quel temps fait-il ? » — « Il pleut. » « Il fait beau. » « Il fait chaud. » « Il fait froid. »
Pour l’heure : « Quelle heure est-il ? » — « Il est huit heures. » « Il est midi. »
Les moments : hier, aujourd’hui, demain.

support.title: Dis avec l’adulte
support.text:
Aujourd’hui, il fait beau.
Hier, il a plu.
Il est huit heures.

lessons.model: Au téléphone, Grand-mère demande : « Quel temps fait-il à Buea ? » Ayuk répond : « Il pleut, et il fait froid. »
lessons.guided: Regarde le ciel et dis le temps qu’il fait. Lis l’heure sur une horloge en français.
lessons.exercise: Il y a beaucoup de soleil. Quel temps fait-il ?
lessons.remediation: Travaille deux expressions : il pleut, il fait beau.
lessons.transfer: Chaque matin, dis en français le temps qu’il fait.
lessons.materials: Une horloge, des images de météo.

practice.prompt: Relie l’image et la phrase.
practice.answer: pluie : il pleut ; soleil : il fait beau ; froid : il fait froid.
practice.explanation: Pour la météo, on dit souvent « il fait ».

practice.prompt: Complète.
practice.text: [[Hier]], il a plu. [[Aujourd’hui]], il fait beau. [[Demain]], il fera chaud.
practice.explanation: hier = yesterday ; aujourd’hui = today ; demain = tomorrow.

practice.prompt: « Il est midi » veut dire…

lessons.title: Electing a class prefect fairly
lessons.objective: Describe how an election works and take part in a fair class election, counting the votes.
lessons.course:
An election lets people choose a leader. In Cameroon there are municipal, legislative and presidential elections. Voters choose freely and secretly; the votes are counted openly and the result is respected.
In class, we can elect a prefect the same way: candidates speak, pupils vote secretly, votes are counted in front of everyone.
lessons.model: The teacher organises an election: three candidates, a box, secret ballots, then counting on the board.
lessons.guided: Organise a class or family election for a small role. Tally the votes and announce the result.
lessons.answer: So that each person chooses freely.
accept: so that each person chooses freely
So that each person chooses freely
lessons.remediation: Do a show-of-hands vote first, then a secret vote.
lessons.transfer: Ask an adult how elections are organised in your municipality.

practice.prompt: Put the steps of an election in order.
practice.explanation: These are the steps of a fair election.

practice.prompt: Bih has 12 votes, Tabi 9, Ngum 7. How many votes in all?
Which election chooses the mayor’s council?

lessons.title: Compost and seed germination
lessons.objective: Make compost to enrich the soil and observe the conditions needed for seeds to germinate.
lessons.course:
Compost is natural manure made from kitchen and garden waste (peels, leaves, grass) that rots in a pit or a heap. It makes the soil rich.
A seed needs water, air and warmth to germinate. We can test it: one seed with water, one without water. Only the one with water germinates.
lessons.model: The adult starts a compost heap with peels and leaves, and plants beans on wet cotton in a tin.
lessons.guided: Put beans on wet cotton and on dry cotton. Observe them each day for a week and write what you see.
lessons.exercise: What does a seed need to germinate?
lessons.remediation: Observe only the wet cotton first.
lessons.transfer: Start a small compost heap at home with your family.
lessons.materials: Beans, cotton, two tins, water, a notebook.

practice.prompt: Which waste can go into compost?
practice.explanation: Plant waste rots and makes compost.

practice.prompt: Put the germination in order.
Write what you saw on day 3 of your experiment.

lessons.title: Reciting a poem on stage
lessons.objective: Recite a short poem with expression and perform on stage.
lessons.course: To recite a poem: learn it line by line, breathe at the end of each line, speak clearly, look at the audience and use gestures that show the meaning.

support.title: A short original poem
support.text:
Our river runs from the hills,
It sings over the stones,
It gives water to the fields,
Please keep it clean, it is our own.

lessons.model: The adult recites the poem slowly with gestures: hands like water, a finger for “please”.
lessons.guided: Learn the poem line by line and recite it to the class or family with gestures.
lessons.exercise: What do we do at the end of each line when reciting?
lessons.remediation: Learn two lines first, then add the others.
lessons.transfer: Recite the poem at a family gathering.

items: Our river runs from the hills,
It gives water to the fields,
Please keep it clean, it is our own.

practice.listen: Our river runs from the hills, it sings over the stones, it gives water to the fields, please keep it clean, it is our own.

practice.prompt: What message does the poem give?
practice.explanation: The last line gives the message.

lessons.title: Forward roll on a soft mat
lessons.objective: Perform a forward roll safely on a soft surface.
lessons.course:
Forward roll: squat, hands flat on the mat, tuck the chin to the chest, push with the feet, roll on the back (not on the head), stand up.
Safety: we roll only on a mat, sand or soft grass, with an adult near; one child at a time.
lessons.model: The adult shows each step slowly, saying “chin to chest!”
lessons.guided: Practise the forward roll on a mat with an adult beside you, three times.
lessons.exercise: Where must the chin be in a forward roll?
lessons.remediation: Roll down a small slope of soft grass first.
lessons.transfer: Show the safety rules of gymnastics to your family.
lessons.materials: A mat or soft grass, an adult.

practice.prompt: Put the forward roll in order.
Where do we practise rolls?
choices: on a mat or soft grass
practice.answer: on a mat or soft grass

practice.prompt: How many children roll at a time?
practice.explanation: One at a time for safety.

lessons.title: Nouns, verbs and adjectives in a conversation
lessons.objective: Use nouns, verbs and adjectives in short sentences and hold a short conversation in the family language.
lessons.course:
In every language, sentences have parts: nouns name people and things (mother, house), verbs show actions (eat, go), adjectives describe (big, red).
In a short conversation we greet, ask a question, answer and say goodbye.
lessons.model: The adult and the child have a short dialogue in the family language: greet, ask “How are you?”, answer, say goodbye.
lessons.guided: With an adult, make three sentences in the family language with a noun, a verb and an adjective. Act a short dialogue.
lessons.exercise: Which word is a verb: house, run, red?
lessons.remediation: Find nouns first: things you can touch.
lessons.transfer: Have a short conversation in the family language every evening.
lessons.materials: An adult who speaks the language.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its part of speech.
practice.answer: mother: noun; eat: verb; big: adjective.

practice.prompt: Put the conversation in order.
Say a sentence in the family language with an adjective.
practice.answer: A sentence with an adjective, said with an adult.

lessons.title: The internet: communicating safely
lessons.objective: Say what the internet is used for and follow safety rules online.
lessons.course:
The internet connects computers and phones of the whole world. We use it to send messages, look for information, learn, watch videos.
Safety rules: use it with an adult, never give your address, school or password to strangers, do not open messages from unknown people, tell an adult if something makes you uncomfortable.
lessons.model: The adult searches for information about Mount Cameroon with the child and talks about safety rules.
lessons.guided: With an adult, look for one piece of information for a school lesson. Make a poster of four safety rules.
lessons.exercise: Should you give your password to a stranger online?
lessons.remediation: Learn two rules first: use it with an adult; keep personal information secret.
lessons.transfer: Explain the safety rules to a younger brother or sister.
lessons.materials: A connected device (with an adult), poster paper.

practice.prompt: Which one is safe online?
choices: telling an adult about a strange message
giving your address to a stranger
practice.answer: telling an adult about a strange message

practice.prompt: Match each use with an example.
practice.answer: communicate: message; learn: read; fun: video.

practice.prompt: Write two safety rules for the internet.
practice.explanation: Keep personal information secret; use it with an adult.
